newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sweeping shake-up for Russian oil giant YUKOS.
newsitem.headline: Sweeping shake-up for Russian oil giant YUKOS.

text.p: Shareholders of Russia's second- largest oil company YUKOS approved a sweeping structural change on Wednesday under which YUKOS's ally, Bank Menatep's Rosprom group, will partially manage the oil giant, Rosprom said.

"YUKOS remains an independent legal entity," Rosprom Chairman and YUKOS Vice-President Mikhail Khodorkovsky told a news conference after an extraordinary shareholders meeting on the matter, which had already been approved in principle.

"YUKOS will maintain functions linked with oil production, refining and marketing. Those functions not connected with these basic tasks will be transferred to the combined (management) structure and carried out by Rosprom," he said.
A YUKOS release said Rosprom would handle financing, investment and strategic planning issues at the oil company.
YUKOS is one of around a dozen vertically-integrated Russian oil companies created over the last few years. Its main production unit is Yuganskneftegaz.
Khodorkovsky said the management change would "give direction" to talks between YUKOS and Amoco of the United States on their giant Priobsk oil production-sharing project.

He said investment bank NM Rothschild and Andersen Consulting would take part in the talks, adding, "This way, we can bring together experienced Amoco specialists and experienced specialists in investment banks.
"We are interested in Amoco's help on technological issues, although we understand that today these services are on the open market and not only Amoco can supply them," he said.
He said Rosprom did not expect to attract foreign investment for the stalled Priobsk project, in which YUKOS and Amoco are still negotiating key issues, before 1998.
Menatep, Rosprom and YUKOS are closely allied.

Menatep-backed unknown company ZAO Laguna manages a 45 percent stake in YUKOS under a 1995 shares-for-loans deal and also has a 33 percent YUKOS stake from a separate tender. The shares-for-loans stake has since been diluted to 33.3 percent via a rights issue.
Menatep has said it has no connection to a second unknown firm, ZAO Monblan, which won a 33.3 percent stake in YUKOS in a tender last year.
